evals.name: plan-mode-cross-authority-contradiction
evals.prompt: /valcraft:valcraft-review — in the Cast project at evals/files/cross-authority/, review docs/plans/2026-08-05-001-feat-t-002-row-limiter-plan.md before implementation.
evals.expected_output: Review selects plan mode, loads the project and Spec-owned contracts (root AGENTS.md, Spec's feature-contract reference, and the cited spec.md, design.md, and tasks.md), and reports material findings. It reports that the plan's EXPORT_ROW_CAP = 5000 violates FR-002, which mandates a 500-row cap, as a P1 citing FR-002 and the concrete input that fires it. It also reports that spec.md and design.md contradict each other on the same cap, that the governing precedence does not separate two artifacts inside specs/, and that the contradiction between the authorities is therefore its own finding rather than one the reviewer settles silently. The canonical source docs/csv-export-prd.md states the 500-row cap, which corroborates the spec and identifies design.md as the document that must change. It routes the plan's "fixture database starts empty" statement to a live-data check demand rather than accepting it as asserted. Findings appear as an auditable table with stable R-IDs, severities, evidence, and a resolution column. The verdict is material findings. No file is edited, no fix is committed, and no review record is written into the repository.
assertions: Review selects plan mode and reads root AGENTS.md, ../valcraft-spec/references/feature-contract.md, and the cited spec.md, design.md, and tasks.md before judging the plan
A material finding reports that the plan's 5000-row cap violates FR-002's 500-row cap and names the concrete export size that fires it
A separate finding reports the spec.md and design.md contradiction on the cap itself, rather than silently adopting either value

The report states that project precedence (accepted ADRs, then specs/, then derived docs/) does not resolve a conflict between two artifacts inside specs/, and resolves it instead from the spec's canonical status and the PRD source
The plan's assumption that the fixture database starts empty is routed to a live-data check demand instead of being accepted as asserted
Findings are presented as a table with stable R-NNN IDs, a severity per finding, evidence, and a resolution column
The verdict is material findings, and the report names the R-IDs a remediation plan must cite
No file in the fixture is edited, no fix is applied or committed, and no raw review record is written into the repository
Any finding the report itself describes as needing no plan or code change is marked P3 rather than escalated to a material level

evals.name: test-strategy-fog-and-span-entries
evals.prompt: /valcraft:valcraft-review — plan-mode review of the FEAT-012 triplet's Test strategy at its pinned commit; every other section already passed. The world is 32 by 16 by 32 blocks and the orbit camera always looks at the world center `(16, 8, 16)`; its azimuth is unrestricted and its polar angle ranges from 10° to 80°; its distance `d` ranges from `minDistance` 30 to `maxDistance` 120. design.md defines fog relative to the camera: `near = d`, `far = d + FOG_SPAN` with `FOG_SPAN = 40`, and each block's fog factor is `smoothstep(near, far, viewDepth)`, where `viewDepth` is the block center's depth along the camera's forward axis. design.md defines a column's surface height as its highest non-air cell, water included; lake columns hold water up to `SEA_LEVEL`. spec.md: AC-008 'At the farthest zoom, from every reachable orbit orientation, every block's fog factor stays below 0.6.' BR-001 'Surface heights of land columns span at least 6 levels.' Test strategy entries: U-FOG (AC-008): 'Observation: at `minDistance`, the opening distance 60, and `maxDistance`, compute the fog factor of every block center with the default orientation (azimuth 0°, polar 60°) and require the maximum below 0.6. Guarded defect: fixed fog distances that swallow the world at maximum zoom. Failing input: setting `far` close to `near`. Positive control: the configured span gives a maximum of 0.39 at all three distances. Domain: every block center, over the camera distance range, covered by its two endpoints and the opening distance.' U-GEN (BR-001): 'Observation: compute every column's surface height from generated storage and require the heights to span at least 6 levels. Guarded defect: a flat heightmap. Failing input: a constant heightmap. Positive control: the app-seed world spans 8 levels. Domain: every column of the generated world, enumerated completely.' Report your findings on these two entries with severity and owner.
evals.expected_output: Two material findings owned by Spec. U-FOG: under camera-relative fog, `viewDepth - near` equals the block's offset from the target along the forward axis, which does not depend on `d`, so the three distances test one state three times; the factor depends on orbit orientation, which AC-008 quantifies over (every azimuth, polar 10° to 80°) and the entry fixes at one orientation. The reviewer reproduces this with a scratch computation, for example identical maxima across distances and a higher maximum at a diagonal orientation: about 0.618 near azimuth 225° and polar 70°, which violates AC-008 while the default orientation gives 0.39. The covering method must be a derived worst-case bound, such as the largest block distance from the target, or selected orientations with a derivation of where the maximum lies; an unjustified sweep would not suffice. U-GEN: the entry's population is every column with water included, while BR-001 covers land columns only, so lake columns at `SEA_LEVEL` can supply span that land lacks; the check must measure land columns only. The triplet does not pass while either finding is open.
assertions: U-FOG is a material finding owned by Spec because the fog factor does not depend on camera distance under this formula, so the three distances test one state
The U-FOG finding names orbit orientation as the free variable AC-008 quantifies over and the entry omits
The reviewer supports the U-FOG finding with a scratch computation or explicit derivation from the formula showing distance independence or orientation dependence
The U-FOG resolution requires a derived worst-case bound or selected orientations with a derivation of where the maximum lies, not a plain orientation sweep
U-GEN is a material finding owned by Spec because its population includes water columns while BR-001 covers land columns only
The triplet does not pass while either finding is open
